evidence.quote: All of the RNase footprint libraries (a total of four for each replicate: ss- and dsRNase treatments, footprint and RNase digestion controls) were sequenced on an Illumina HiSeq2000 using the standard protocols for 50-bp single-read sequencing.

Specifically, the read coverage was calculated for each base position in the genome and a Poisson test was used to compute an enrichment score for the footprint versus RNase digestion control libraries (Additional file 1).
These sequences can be used to identify the interacting proteins so that their effects on post-transcriptional regulation can be further studied.
evidence.rationale: The paper places identification of interacting proteins as further use of the recovered RNA sequences, and the assigned schematic depicts neither a protein-specific capture nor a protein-identity reporter. Thus these sequence reads localize protected RNA without directly encoding the protecting protein identity.

evidence.quote: This is not surprising, given that formaldehyde both has a longer range than UV and can also stabilize more transient and indirect interactions.

No protein-identity reporter is depicted, and formaldehyde can capture indirect interactions, so reads do not identify the protecting RBP or establish a direct contact. The schematic ends at sequencing; PPS calling is interpretation supported by the paper rather than an additional depicted operation.
